title: Make a household utility response card

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A utility response card separates extent of disruption, authoritative service information, permitted user action and a stop point. It does not authorize opening equipment or improvising safety tests.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Fictional internet case: laptop cannot load pages, but a phone on the same home Wi-Fi can. Provider status page reports no known area outage, not a guarantee. Exact fictional laptop help card permits checking Wi-Fi selection and toggling that device’s Wi-Fi once; it does not authorize router reset or opening hardware. Laptop shows it is connected to an old guest network. No smoke, heat or electrical concern is present.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Draw a decision sequence using these states and the one permitted user action. State what would remain unknown if it fails.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: Every device loses connection and the provider confirms an outage with no restoration time. Can a local reboot be reported as restoring service before a check?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The working phone narrows the known issue to the laptop/route, not necessarily the provider. Select the correct authorized network without disclosing credentials; the help card allows one device-level toggle if needed. Later fiction: connection still fails; contact appropriate support with the observed states, not repeated resets. Partial: inspect outage status only. Incorrect: reset shared equipment without authority or open covers.
criteria: The fault sequence follows actual observations
Only authorized user-level actions are chosen
Stop and escalation conditions are concrete

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: No. Preserve the outage and unknown restoration, use a suitable available alternative if needed and verify actual return. A plan or reboot attempt is not restored service.
